international.canonicalTopic: India–Liberia Group of Friends on shipping and seafarer safety
international.headline: India and Liberia launch Group of Friends for shipping and seafarer safety
facts: India and Liberia launched the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers in New York on 2026-09-25 during the High-Level Week of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
The group aims to address attacks on commercial ships and civilian seafarers along critical maritime routes and strengthen their safety and security.
The notes identify India as a major supplier of seafarers and Liberia as the operator of the world’s largest ship registry by tonnage.
The UN General Assembly is headquartered in New York, has 193 members and follows the principle of one country, one vote.
international.summary: India and Liberia launched a UN-related grouping to focus on the safety and security of commercial shipping and civilian seafarers.
international.staticLink: A ship registry records commercial vessels under a country’s authority and oversees their legal and technical standards.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The group was launched during the 81st UNGA High-Level Week; the UNGA has 193 members and follows one country, one vote.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the importance of maritime security and protection of seafarers to global trade and international governance.

national.canonicalTopic: India signs United Nations Convention against Cybercrime
national.headline: India signs the UN Convention against Cybercrime
facts: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime for India in New York on September 25, 2026, during the 81st UN General Assembly.
The convention is described as the first comprehensive global treaty designed to prevent and combat cybercrime through international cooperation.
It provides a legal framework for countries to strengthen coordination against transnational cybercrime.
The UN General Assembly has 193 members and is headquartered in New York.
national.summary: India signed a global convention intended to strengthen international cooperation and legal coordination in tackling transnational cybercrime.
national.staticLink: International cooperation against cybercrime; United Nations General Assembly.
national.prelimsTakeaway: India signed the convention on 2026-09-25 in New York; the notes describe it as the first comprehensive global cybercrime treaty.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the importance of cross-border cooperation and legal frameworks in combating transnational cybercrime.

national.canonicalTopic: Sarah Peluse selected for the SASTRA Ramanujan Prize 2026
national.headline: Sarah Peluse selected for the 2026 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize
facts: Stanford University Associate Professor of Mathematics Sarah Peluse was selected for the SASTRA Ramanujan Prize–2026 on September 25, 2026.
The selection recognises research in analytic number theory, additive combinatorics, combinatorial geometry and group theory.
The prize is for mathematicians aged 32 or below and carries USD 10,000.
The award is scheduled to be presented on December 22, 2026, at SASTRA University in Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu.
The prize was instituted in 2005; December 22 is the birth anniversary of Srinivasa Ramanujan and is observed as National Mathematics Day in India.
national.summary: Sarah Peluse was selected for the 2026 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize for research in several areas of mathematics.

national.prelimsTakeaway: The SASTRA Ramanujan Prize is for mathematicians aged 32 or below and carries USD 10,000; it is presented by SASTRA University.

national.headline: Make in India marks 12 years
facts: Make in India was launched on 2014-09-25 and marked 12 years on 2026-09-25; its objectives include domestic manufacturing, investment, exports and industrial competitiveness.
The initiative covers 27 sectors: 15 manufacturing and 12 service sectors.
The notes state that India received USD 94.53 billion in FDI in 2025–26 and that cumulative FDI from 2014–15 to 2025–26 reached USD 843 billion.

Electronics production rose from around ₹1.9 lakh crore in 2014–15 to an estimated ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26; mobile phone manufacturing increased from ₹18,000 crore to ₹6.27 lakh crore over the same period.
The notes describe India as the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer by production volume.
The nodal department is the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
national.summary: Make in India marked 12 years with a focus on manufacturing, investment, exports and competitiveness. The notes cite growth in FDI, electronics production and mobile-phone manufacturing.
national.staticLink: Industrial policy, foreign direct investment and domestic value addition.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The initiative covers 27 sectors—15 manufacturing and 12 services—and is administered by DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the initiative’s contribution to manufacturing capacity, investment, exports and domestic value addition, alongside the challenges of competitiveness.
